transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I have this intense, over-the-top fear of being up high in tall buildings that doesn’t match what I know is the actual risk, and it’s starting to interfere with my work. I finally decided to seek help because it's making it really difficult to do my job lately.
Is this intense fear strictly related to heights, or do you also feel anxious in other situations like crowded places, public transit, or open spaces where escape might be difficult?

No, it is strictly limited to heights, high buildings, glass elevators, and exposed high viewpoints. I don't feel anxious at all in crowded places, on public transit, or in open spaces, as long as I'm close to the ground.
How long have you been experiencing this intense fear of heights?

I’ve always had a mild uneasiness with heights, like when hiking, but I could easily manage it back then. It became a severe, consistent problem about seven months ago when I got promoted into a role requiring me to run trainings in high-rise offices.
When you are faced with heights or high-rise buildings, do you experience an immediate wave of intense anxiety or panic every single time?

Yes, absolutely every single time. As soon as I know I have to go to a high floor, my heart starts pounding, my hands get sweaty, and I feel lightheaded before I even step inside. If I can't get out of it, I just have to grit my teeth and endure a constant wave of fear the entire time I'm up there.

latest_inference.note: The candidate remains F40.2 (Specific phobia). The patient's symptoms meet all diagnostic criteria: an intense, disproportionate fear of heights (tall buildings/elevators), immediate anxiety/panic symptoms upon exposure, active avoidance or endurance with intense distress, a duration of over 6 months (7 months), and significant occupational impairment. Other diagnoses like agoraphobia have been ruled out. Therefore, we can confidently finalize the diagnosis.
